sources.title: Simon K. Donaldson, The ADHM construction of Yang-Mills instantons
sources.locator: Printed pp. 3–12 (PDF pp. 3–12): ADHM data, twistor/Ward transform, monad reconstruction, explicit matrix normalization, and Dirac inverse. Full source limit and exact item disposition are recorded in batch-60 notes after inspection.

contents.name: §2, ADHM data and its framed U(r) instanton problem, printed p. 3
contents.support: The source fixes a framed U(r) bundle on S4, instanton number, and the linear-map construction. Its symbols and self-duality orientation are translated explicitly in the local definition.

contents.name: §3, twistor space and Ward correspondence, printed pp. 4–5
contents.support: The source constructs the bundle over the space of real twistor lines and gives both transform directions. It is used as a route map; its local proof supplies are stated explicitly rather than treating the exposition as a complete local proof.

contents.name: §4–5, monad reconstruction and vanishing, printed pp. 6–10
contents.support: The source gives the Barth–Hulek vanishing hypotheses, Beilinson/Koszul reconstruction, and the coupled Laplace vanishing route. It invokes Penrose transform, Serre duality, and the Barth–Hulek theorem; those inputs are not silently promoted to local proofs.

contents.name: §6, explicit matrix description, printed pp. 10–11
contents.support: The source displays the quaternionic block matrix and equations; the proposed entrywise-conjugation translation is separately disproved in a local matrix check, so the full block/regularity interface remains escalated.

contents.name: §§2–6, completeness of the ADHM construction, printed pp. 3–11
contents.support: The source states the framed ADHM route. Its matrix, GAGA and Ward steps are treated as local proof obligations; current batch-59 GAGA and P2 carriers are conditional and escalated.

contents.name: §2, charge normalization and framed U(N) data, printed p. 3
contents.support: Donaldson fixes the framed U(r) instanton number and Chern-class normalization; the determinant ASD-line, framing and U(N) trace proof is supplied locally.

contents.name: §3, line sections and first-neighbourhood extension, printed pp. 4–5
contents.support: Donaldson describes the section bundle and first-neighbourhood construction; family base-change surjectivity remains an explicit local hypothesis.

contents.name: §5, coupled Laplace equation and positive scalar term, printed p. 8
contents.support: The source gives the coupled Laplace operator and positive-curvature vanishing route; the compact integration-by-parts proof is written locally.

contents.name: §5, Penrose transform to the coupled Laplace equation, printed pp. 8–9
contents.support: The source states the transform and equation but does not prove the transform injection; the local lemma is explicitly conditional on that input.

contents.name: §6, printed pp. 10–11, source matrix notation and equations (8)–(9)
contents.support: The local definition records the source matrices and equations with the displayed P and Q map dimensions.

contents.name: §6, printed pp. 10–11, equations (8)–(9)
contents.support: Exact conjugation of the source equations is compared with the run raw real moment; an explicit 2x2 source solution gives a nonzero discrepancy. The separate full-rank condition is not claimed for that check.

contents.name: §§4–5, printed pp. 6–10, monad coefficient spaces
contents.support: The source gives the normalized monad dimensions and its charge interpretation; the local K-class and twistor orientation calculation are supplied in the item.

contents.name: §2, printed p. 3, charge-zero ASD boundary
contents.support: The source fixes instanton charge; the zero-charge implication and framing uniqueness are proved locally using the ready action-bound and simple-connectivity suppliers.

sources.title: Hiraku Nakajima and Kota Yoshioka, Lectures on Instanton Counting
sources.locator: §3.1, printed pp. 17–19: framed torsion-free sheaves, their locally-free locus, the stated framed SU(r) ASD identification, and torus conventions. The authors direct readers to cited references for details; this is not recorded as a full local proof.

contents.name: §3.1, framed sheaves and their locally-free locus, printed pp. 17–19
contents.support: The source states that the locally-free locus in framed-sheaf moduli is the framed SU(r) ASD moduli. It cites Donaldson and is recorded as an exact source interface, not as a local proof of the ADHM comparison.

contents.name: §3.1, framing forces c1=0, printed p. 17
contents.support: The source states the c1=0 consequence of framing at infinity. The U(N) determinant connection and k=-q_N trace normalization are separately proved under the round-S4 hypotheses.

contents.name: §3.1, printed pp. 17–19, framed torsion-free sheaf and locally-free locus
contents.support: The source distinguishes framed torsion-free sheaves from their locally-free locus; the N=k=1 point-ideal monad and positive-FI equations are checked explicitly in the example.
